## 🔴 Errors (will cause build failures or incorrect behavior)

### 🔴 E1 — `$(TargetFramework)` condition in `Directory.Build.props` is dead code (AP-21)
**File:** `Directory.Build.props`, line 10

```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(TargetFramework)' == 'net8.0'">
  <GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>
</PropertyGroup>
```

For single-targeting projects (all projects in this solution), `$(TargetFramework)` is **empty** during `.props` evaluation. The outer-loop evaluation sets `$(TargetFrameworks)` (plural), dispatches the inner loop which sets `$(TargetFramework)` — but `.props` files are imported *before* that dispatch. This condition **never matches**, so `GenerateDocumentationFile` is never set to `true`.

**Fix:** Move this to `Directory.Build.targets`, which is evaluated after the TFM is resolved:
```xml
<!-- In Directory.Build.targets -->
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(TargetFramework)' == 'net8.0'">
  <GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>
</PropertyGroup>
```

---

### 🔴 E2 — Property defaults in `Directory.Build.targets` override project-level settings
**File:** `Directory.Build.targets`, lines 6–11

```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
  <Company>Contoso</Company>
  <Authors>Build Team</Authors>
  <Copyright>Copyright 2024 Contoso</Copyright>
</PropertyGroup>
```

Import order is: `Directory.Build.props` → `*.csproj` → SDK `.targets` → `Directory.Build.targets`. Because `.targets` is evaluated **after** the project file, `TreatWarningsAsErrors=true` silently stomps `LibB.csproj`'s explicit `TreatWarningsAsErrors=false` (line 13). LibB's authors believe warnings aren't errors, but they are — this is a correctness trap.

**Fix:** Move these to `Directory.Build.props` as conditional defaults so projects can override:
```xml
<!-- In Directory.Build.props -->
<PropertyGroup>
  <TreatWarningsAsErrors Condition="'$(TreatWarningsAsErrors)' == ''">true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
  <Company>Contoso</Company>
  <Authors>Build Team</Authors>
  <Copyright>Copyright 2024 Contoso</Copyright>
</PropertyGroup>
```

### 🔴 E3 — `DefineConstants` overwrites SDK defaults
**File:** `LibA/LibA.csproj`, line 14

```xml
<DefineConstants>ENABLE_LOGGING</DefineConstants>
```

This **replaces** the default `DefineConstants` value (which includes `TRACE` and, for Debug, `DEBUG`). Any `#if DEBUG` or `#if TRACE` code silently stops working.

**Fix:** Append instead of replace:
```xml
<DefineConstants>$(DefineConstants);ENABLE_LOGGING</DefineConstants>
```

---

### 🔴 E4 — Unquoted condition value
**File:** `LibA/LibA.csproj`, line 13

```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="$(Configuration) == Debug">
```

The condition is missing quotes. If `$(Configuration)` is empty or contains spaces, this evaluates incorrectly or errors. MSBuild best practice requires quoting both sides.

**Fix:**
```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(Configuration)' == 'Debug'">
```

### 🔴 E5 — F# compile order wrong in `BrokenOrder.fsproj`
**File:** `fsharp/BrokenOrder/BrokenOrder.fsproj`, lines 7–9

```xml
<Compile Include="Services.fs" />
<Compile Include="Domain.fs" />
<Compile Include="Program.fs" />

F# is **order-dependent** — a file can only reference types/modules defined in files listed *above* it. `Services.fs` opens `BrokenOrder.Domain`, but `Domain.fs` is listed **after** `Services.fs`. This will produce a compile error like `FS0039: The namespace 'Domain' is not defined`.

Compare with `OrderService.fsproj` which has the correct order: `Domain.fs` → `Services.fs` → `Program.fs`.

**Fix:** Reorder to match the dependency graph:
```xml
<Compile Include="Domain.fs" />
<Compile Include="Services.fs" />
<Compile Include="Program.fs" />
```

### 🔴 E6 — Publish-on-build re-invokes the same project, causing double build + file race
**File:** `LibA/LibA.csproj`, lines 43–45

```xml
<Target Name="PublishOnBuild" AfterTargets="Build">

</Target>

This forks a **second evaluation** of LibA with global property `{_IsPublishing=true}`, creating a distinct project instance that writes to the same `OutputPath`/`IntermediateOutputPath`. The two instances race writing the same files, causing intermittent `NETSDK1packages` and "file in use" errors — especially under parallel builds. It also doubles the build time for LibA.

**Fix:** Use `DependsOnTargets` to run Publish in the *same* project instance:
```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <BuildDependsOn>$(BuildDependsOn);PublishAfterBuild</BuildDependsOn>
</PropertyGroup>
<Target Name="PublishAfterBuild" Condition="'$(DesignTimeBuild)' != 'true'">
  <!-- Publish logic here, in the same instance -->
